MI Agent, Medical Imaging Agent
MI Agent Workflow

You started two agents in the first lab. What did they do, where did they record their work, and how can you inspect their results?

In this lesson, follow the work from your instructions to the experiment records and image predictions. Start with the research and experiment loop for ImageCAS, then follow the architecture experiments for ImageCHD.

By the end of this lab, you will be able to:

  • Connect the two original prompts to the work recorded by each agent.
  • Use the challenge files to understand task facts, decisions, and execution.
  • Follow an experiment from its intent to its validation results and viewer.
  • Compare training curves with the saved metrics and prediction overlays.
  • Ask the agent an evidence-based question about its next experiment.

0. Recall the two tasks

In lesson 01, you launched ImageCAS first and ImageCHD second. Below are the original prompts. Read them as a reminder of the tasks already running; you do not need to launch them again.

First agent: ImageCAS

:/auto Check how this environment is setup and what skills are available to you. Read AGENTS.md and follow its workflow,  use `/data/ImageCAS_lab` challenge and run for 90 minutes or till you reach dice of 0.9.

This task asks the agent to inspect the environment, discover its skills, and follow the challenge workflow. Its stopping condition is Dice 0.90 or 90 minutes.

Second agent: ImageCHD

:/auto Read AGENTS.md and follow its workflow and referenced skills. Using only /data/ImageCHD_lab as a challenge, skip literature survey, skip crticism, start immediately by training different network architectures in order: MONAI SegResNet, Unet and nvsegment-finetune. Minimize the code you write by always use your skills and tools. before writing code check if monai has a library or function to do it.  Run decision-bearing experiments until validation Dice reaches 0.90 or 55 minutes have elapsed. Limit each experiment to 10 epochs and validate only at epochs 5 and 10. Use the managed launcher and its measured shared-GPU allowance. Finish with the best saved validation result in NiiVue and a concise experiment summary, then stop.

This task supplies a more specific experiment plan: skip literature and criticism, try the named architectures in order, cap each experiment at 10 epochs, and validate at epochs 5 and 10. Stop when validation Dice reaches 0.90 or 55 minutes have elapsed, then present the best saved validation result and summary.

We will inspect CAS first to follow the research, decisions, experiments, and results viewer. Then we will review the architecture experiments for CHD.

1. Check your agents' progress

1.1 Ask the agent about experiment status

Explore your agent's work by asking questions in your own words. Here are some ideas:

  • Ask about the results.
  • Ask about the status of the experiments.
  • Ask whether anything else is still running.
  • Ask what score each experiment achieved.

Use the answers to decide what you want to explore next, and ask follow-up questions.

To connect the answers to the saved records, ask your agent:

Explain how the files in my challenge folder connect the original prompt to the current experiments. Point me to the task definition, dashboard, active baseline, and one experiment record.
Expected output of the agent should be

The agent should identify your actual challenge folder and link its records. Its explanation should connect the original task to the current focus, planned and running jobs, the selected baseline, and one experiment's intent and outcome. Use this file map to interpret the answer:

FileQuestion it answers
challenge.mdWhat is the task, dataset, split, metric, and evaluation contract?
state.mdWhat is the current focus and what evidence is needed next?
dashboard.mdWhat is planned, running, completed, or blocked? What resources and best results are recorded?
trajectory.mdWhich consequential decisions or human instructions changed the direction?
literature.md / candidates.mdWhat evidence and alternatives support the chosen solution?
baselines/<baseline>/baseline.mdWhat is this solution direction, its implementation plan, and its exploration map?
runs/<experiment>/experiment.mdWhat was the pre-run intent, what happened, and what decision followed?
result_viewer.htmlWhat do the saved predictions look like on individual cases?

Run folders sit inside their baseline. Long logs, checkpoints, predictions, and viewers are linked artifacts; the main records help you find and interpret them.

The agent should distinguish recorded results from planned work. A queued job or an experiment intent is not a completed result.

2. First project: walk through ImageCAS

Open the MIAgent Viewer in a new tab. In the file tree, expand challenge, then imagecas_lab. Follow how the agent moved from understanding the challenge to researching, selecting, and refining a solution.

2.1 Read the task and evaluation contract

Open challenge.md. Locate the target structure, data path, train/validation split, metric aggregation, and stopping condition.

The task shown is coronary artery segmentation on cardiac CT. Its metric is calculated per validation case and then averaged across the five cases. Keep the local lab task distinct from results reported on other dataset versions or benchmark splits.

2.2 Follow the research evidence

Open literature.md. Start with the agent's problem decomposition and proposed pipeline, then read how the evidence supports or challenges that proposal.

Focus on how evidence affects decisions. Check whether a cited result uses a comparable task and evaluation, whether code or weights are available, and whether a proposed method fits the compute budget. The numbers in these notes are research references, not scores achieved by this lab run.

2.3 Inspect the critique and its limitations

Expand critics and read the available critique. Look for weak evidence, assumptions, and checks that could change the selected method.

In this example, the critique questions evidence for the selected architecture, the compute estimates behind alternative selection, and uncertainty in the labels. Inspect your run's record to see which checks were proposed and whether later experiments resolved them.

2.4 Trace the consequential decisions

Open trajectory.md. Follow the original human instruction, candidate selection, and implementation-plan decision. Use the evidence links to find the full reasoning in its owning record.

Then open the selected baseline's baseline.md to inspect its implementation plan and exploration map.

2.5 Follow the experiments

Open dashboard.md. Read the snapshot for the target, stop condition, compute allowance, and active baseline. Then inspect the job tables and local runtime telemetry.

For each comparison, ask what changed, which earlier run it compares against, and what the validation evidence says. Check the recorded outcome before treating an improvement as established.

Walk me through the ImageCAS decisions from the original task to the current best recorded validation run. Explain how the literature and critique affected the baseline, what changed between experiments, and why the next experiment was chosen. Link the supporting records.

2.6 Inspect the coronary artery predictions

Follow a completed CAS experiment's viewer link, or expand its result_viewers folder and open result_viewer.html. Select a case from the list.

  1. Confirm the selected case and experiment name.
  2. Switch between Prediction and Ground truth on the same case and location.
  3. Use Difference to inspect disagreement between the saved labels and prediction.
  4. Adjust Overlay opacity and CT contrast so you can see both the image and labels.
  5. Inspect axial, sagittal, and coronal views; use the volume rendering for spatial context.
  6. Open Case metrics and compare several cases, including a weaker one.

Follow the labeled structures across adjacent slices and planes. Compare the prediction and reference for missing branches, extra regions, or gaps. Use several cases rather than judging the experiment from a single favorable image.

3. Second project: walk through ImageCHD

3.1 Open the challenge dashboard

In the same file tree, expand imagechd_lab and select dashboard.md. Now follow the architecture experiments specified in the second prompt.

Find the smoke test, GPU profiling step, and architecture experiments. In this capture, the smoke and GPU optimization runs are completed, SegResNet is running, and UNet and NVSegment fine-tuning are queued. The completed-runs table has no validation result listed yet.

A smoke test checks that the pipeline and viewer work. Profiling measures resource needs before expensive training. Neither establishes final model quality. The agent controls the workflow in the miagent container; admitted GPU jobs execute in the training container.

3.2 Inspect one experiment's intent

Expand the active baseline and its runs folder. Open an experiment.md record and read its Intent. Find the question, comparator, and intervention before looking for an outcome.

In this example, the UNet experiment asks whether it can beat or approach SegResNet under the same 10-epoch schedule. Read the outcome when available to learn whether the planned comparison actually completed.

For ImageCHD, which architectures completed, which are still queued or failed, and what is the best saved validation result? Link the experiment records and viewer. Distinguish completed evidence from planned comparisons.

3.3 Open the validation viewer

Follow a completed experiment's viewer link, or expand its result_viewers folder and open result_viewer.html. Select a case from the list.

Use the viewer controls introduced in the CAS walkthrough: compare Prediction, Ground truth, and Difference; adjust Overlay opacity and CT contrast; and inspect multiple planes and cases. Confirm the selected experiment before interpreting its scores.

4. Compare experiments with MLflow and TensorBoard

At the top of the MIAgent Viewer, click MLflow or TensorBoard. The screenshot below highlights where to find these links.

4.1 Find the runs in MLflow

Select the experiment group matching your challenge and baseline, then open a run. Inspect its available parameters, metrics, duration, and artifacts. Match the run name to the challenge's experiment record.

4.2 Read the curves in TensorBoard

Filter the run list to the experiments you want to compare. Inspect training loss, learning rate, and validation Dice. Check the horizontal axis and smoothing setting when interpreting the curves.

Lower training loss alone does not establish better validation performance. Compare runs under a consistent split and metric, check which checkpoint produced the reported score, and inspect the corresponding prediction viewer.

Compare two completed runs from the same challenge. What changed, how did validation Dice change, and what do the saved predictions show? Use the experiment records and available tracking metrics, and explain any limits to the comparison.
